extracted.intended_audience: prospective grant applicants (nonprofits/organizations), grantees, and foundation program staff/consultants
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the Doris Duke Foundation's process for developing initiatives, awarding grants, the criteria considered in funding decisions, and the evaluation strategies used to assess grants and programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project addresses significant funding gap or critical opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address a significant funding gap or support a critical opportunity related to the foundation's mission?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a core consideration applied across DDF programs, even though award methods differ by program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with applicant and foundation program goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the project designed to achieve both the objectives of the applicant organization and the program goals of the foundation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation considers both organizational objectives and how the project advances DDF program goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for long-term impact
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the project's potential for long-term impact in terms of replication, reach, visibility or changes in the field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers measurable and durable effects such as replication, expanded reach, increased visibility, or systemic change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant organizational capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the applicant organization have the capacity to effectively execute the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capacity assessments inform decisions about an organization's ability to deliver proposed outputs and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to leverage additional resources
rubrics_metrics.description: What opportunity exists to leverage additional resources as a result of DDF funding?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers whether DDF funds can attract or catalyze other funding, partnerships, or in-kind support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation objective: determine whether grants are meeting objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: To help the foundation determine whether its grants are meeting their objectives; more specifically, to determine whether grants are achieving their intended outcomes and whether the grantmaking strategies the foundation has employed are helping DDF meet its program objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing assessments focus on outcomes and the effectiveness of grantmaking strategies in advancing program objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation objective: inform future decision-making and program design
rubrics_metrics.description: To inform future decision-making and to guide the foundation's work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program evaluations help DDF determine whether to continue, modify or discontinue a particular grantmaking strategy or initiative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and Assessment (ongoing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Through site visits, grantee consultations and review of annual progress reports, staff determines compliance with grant agreements and assesses initial outputs, outcomes and indicators that are likely to correlate with the future impact of the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ongoing process conducted by internal staff and, as needed, outside consultants; focuses on compliance and early indicators of impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of Initiatives (intensive review)
rubrics_metrics.description: A specific initiative or cluster of related grants is selected for a more intensive review to determine whether funded initiatives appear to be achieving their desired goals and objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usually involves outside consultants and is conducted every three to five years; results inform whether initiative design needs refinement or continued funding is merited.

rubrics_metrics.name: External Program Review (field-level review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff analyzes a field, or sectors within a field, to identify potential funding opportunities and returns approximately every five years to conduct a systematic review of DDF-supported fields and the foundation's role within them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conducted about every five years using outside consultants and/or field experts; findings are used to refine, redesign, continue or eliminate program strategies and to repeat the evaluation cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant award methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are awarded in a variety of ways, including foundation-initiated invitations to apply, regranting competitions administered by service organizations and competitions run using request-for-proposal processes; occasionally opportunistic grants are supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While there are overarching similarities, each DDF program approaches grantmaking in a unique way; method of awarding may affect application process and evaluation specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiative development through program staff research
rubrics_metrics.description: Program staff conducts extensive research to identify gaps or needs that the foundation can address; this research typically leads to development of a grant initiative supporting related grants to advance a specific goal or objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The analysis of fields and sectors is the starting point for creating initiatives and informs subsequent evaluation and refinement.
